  "text": "When the repair shop closed, Miriam brought home the drawer of unclaimed keys.

Her son asked what she meant to do with them.

“Give people another chance,” she said.

She put a notice in the bakery window. Keys from Bell Street Repairs. Please describe.

The first caller wanted a bicycle lock key with a red cap. Miriam spread the keys on a tea towel and found three red caps, none belonging to a bicycle lock.

“Sorry,” she told him.

“That’s all right. I cut it off years ago.”

A woman collected two small keys on a brass ring. She tried them in a cashbox she had brought in her shopping bag. The lid opened. Inside were a receipt and a rubber band.

“I wondered,” the woman said.

By November, Miriam had returned eleven keys. The others filled a biscuit tin beneath the telephone.

One afternoon she found a paper tag among them. Her husband’s handwriting: Mrs Vale. Back door. Thursday.

Mrs Vale had moved into sheltered housing before he died. Miriam rang her anyway.

“Oh, that door,” Mrs Vale said. “You had to lift it with your knee.”

They spoke for twenty minutes.

Afterwards, Miriam wrote Mrs Vale’s new address on the back of the tag. She put it beside the telephone rather than in the tin.

Her son visited on Sunday. He lifted the tin to make room for his cup.

“Still keeping these?”

“For now.”

He set it on the windowsill. When he left, she moved it back, within reach of her chair."
